special_flags: Gentle intensity preference: keep SLOW rate and prioritize comfort
If any warmth/headache/nausea occurs, slow or pause and reassess

preflight_checks: Confirm patient identity: name + DOB (or clinic ID).
Confirm consent for IV session and selected option (Glow Antioxidant).
Baseline vitals required: BP, HR, SpO2, Temp (confirm Temp is not fever-range; if systemic temp available, ensure <37.5°C).
Baseline symptoms required: dizziness (yes/no), nausea (yes/no), anxiety/palpitations (yes/no), headache (yes/no).
Hard-stop screen: confirm NO chest pain now, NO shortness of breath now, NO fainting episode today, NO confusion or severe weakness now.
Confirm safety screen: not pregnant/breastfeeding; no kidney disease; no G6PD deficiency; no severe allergy/anaphylaxis history; no asthma; no seizure history.
Confirm no current fever/infection symptoms today.
setup_steps: Gather supplies: IV cannula (20–24G as appropriate), tourniquet, antiseptic prep, sterile gauze, transparent dressing, extension set, saline flushes, sharps container, gloves, IV administration set, IV stand, labels/marker, and infusion pump if available for controlled SLOW delivery.
Prepare 250 ml Normal Saline (0.9%) bag; label with patient name/ID, date/time, and additives: Vitamin C (High Dose) 2000 mg + Glutathione 1200 mg + Glycine 500 mg.
Add ingredients using aseptic technique; gently invert to mix; visually inspect bag for clarity/particulates/leaks.
Prime IV tubing with the prepared bag; remove air from line.
Establish IV access; secure cannula with transparent dressing; confirm patency with saline flush and check for pain/swelling.
administration_steps: Start infusion at SLOW rate with planned minimum duration 60 minutes for 250 ml; adjust slower if patient prefers or if any discomfort occurs.
At start, explain expected sensations and to report immediately: chest tightness, shortness of breath, dizziness, nausea, headache, flushing/warmth, or IV site burning/pain.
If mild warmth or mild headache occurs: reduce rate and continue with comfort checks; offer oral water if appropriate.
If moderate nausea, moderate dizziness, moderate headache, IV site pain/burning, or patient asks to stop: pause infusion and reassess before resuming at a slower rate.
If infiltration suspected (swelling, pain, coolness at site): stop infusion, disconnect, manage site per clinic policy, and restart in a new vein only if clinically appropriate.
Complete infusion; flush line per clinic policy; discontinue IV and apply pressure dressing when stable.

baseline_measurements: Record baseline BP, HR, SpO2, Temp.
Record baseline symptoms: dizziness, nausea, anxiety/palpitations, headache.
Confirm hard-stop symptoms are absent: chest pain now, shortness of breath now, fainting today, confusion/severe weakness now.
during_infusion_checks: Comfort check every 10–15 min (ask about nausea, headache, dizziness, warmth/flushing, anxiety/palpitations).
IV site check every 10–15 min (pain, burning, swelling, redness, leakage).
If any symptoms develop, re-check BP/HR/SpO2 as needed and adjust rate accordingly.
stop_rules: Stop immediately and call clinician if: chest pain.
Stop immediately and call clinician if: shortness of breath.
Stop immediately and call clinician if: fainting / near-fainting.
Stop immediately and call clinician if: rapidly worsening symptoms.
escalation_rules: Pause and reassess if: moderate nausea.
Pause and reassess if: moderate dizziness.
Pause and reassess if: moderate headache.
Pause and reassess if: IV site pain/burning.
Pause and reassess if: patient asks to stop.

post_care: Re-check end-of-session vitals: BP, HR, SpO2.
Assess patient’s overall tolerance and symptom status before discharge (dizziness, nausea, headache, palpitations).

Provide basic aftercare: encourage oral hydration as tolerated; advise to avoid strenuous activity if lightheaded; keep dressing on per clinic policy; report delayed rash, swelling, shortness of breath, or worsening symptoms to clinic/urgent care per policy.
documentation: carrier + bag size: 250 ml Normal Saline (0.9%).
all additives and final doses actually administered: Vitamin C (High Dose) 2000 mg; Glutathione 1200 mg; Glycine 500 mg.
start time, end time, total duration (target 60 minutes) and any pauses.
rate profile used (SLOW) and any rate changes with reasons.
baseline vitals + end vitals (BP/HR/SpO2/Temp baseline; BP/HR/SpO2 end).
any symptoms during infusion and actions taken (slowdown/pause/stop, vitals re-checks).
constraints status + any restrictions applied (Vitamin C within cap; Glutathione at/above floor; SLOW for gentle preference).
clinician_signoff_required_if: Any hard-stop symptom occurs (chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting/near-fainting, rapidly worsening symptoms).
Any suspected allergic reaction or anaphylaxis concern.
IV infiltration/extravasation requiring clinical decision to restart or discontinue.
Baseline vitals are outside clinic policy thresholds or systemic temperature is ≥37.5°C.
Patient requests to stop early or has persistent moderate symptoms despite rate reduction.
